5.  Outbound: Submit Request

   An Agent's only outbound action is dropping an inert request file
   into its Namespace.  The file carries no send capability; the Runtime
   enforces policy before anything leaves.

   A Submit Request is written to <volume-root>/<agent-id>/outbound/
   req-<id>.json as a JSON text [RFC8259].  Its Sidecar bytes, if any,
   are written first, into req-<id>.attachments/, one blob per
   Descriptor, named by that Descriptor's 0-based array index
   (Section 4.1, commit sentinel).

















Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 22]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "req_id": "00000001",
     "agent_id": "agent.research",
     "ts": "2026-07-20T04:10:56Z",
     "in_reply_to": "1721457600000000000-4242",
     "draft": {
       "to": ["owner@example.com"],
       "cc": [],
       "subject": "Run report",
       "body_text": "The run finished; details below.",
       "reply_to_message_id": null,
       "attachments": [
         {
           "filename": "report.pdf",
           "media_type": "application/pdf",
           "size_bytes": 48213,
           "sha256": "970e441b6c4ecd37abf2541e1276c680bdec8481cef9368ff\
       1d010fd6b784b07"
         }
       ]
     }
   }

      Figure 2: draft/examples/submit-request.json (illustrative — not
                                 a fixture)

   The normative shape is Appendix A.  The Submit Request envelope is
   *closed*: additionalProperties is false at every level, and a Runtime
   MUST reject a request carrying any unrecognized member.  Section 11.1
   explains why this direction is closed while the Runtime-authored
   artifacts are open.

5.1.  Field semantics and obligations

   *  *contract_version* (REQUIRED) is the wire major version, the
      string "2" at this document version.  A Runtime MUST check it
      before schema validation and MUST fail closed on an absent, lower,
      or higher major (Section 11.1).










Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 23]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *req_id* (REQUIRED) is *monotonic per Namespace* and MUST NOT be
      reused across the drop-box's life; derive it from max(pending,
      processed, results) + 1.  Reuse collides message identifiers and
      triggers provider-side idempotency deduplication. req_id is pinned
      to a filename-safe character set by the schema, but it is not the
      path authority: the Runtime derives the path identifier from the
      validated filename (Section 4.1).

   *  *agent_id* (OPTIONAL), if present, MUST match the Namespace the
      request was found in, and a Runtime MUST reject a mismatch.  It is
      never the attribution source (Section 4.1).

   *  *ts* (OPTIONAL) is the Connector's timestamp for the request.  It
      is Agent-authored and therefore advisory.

   *  *in_reply_to* (OPTIONAL) correlates this request with prior
      inbound work.  It carries either a Runtime-minted notice_id or a
      mail message identifier [RFC5322].  It is a *hint from an
      untrusted party* and MUST NOT by itself widen what the request is
      permitted to do — the same posture Section 8 fixes for task_id.

   *  The Runtime derives the message identity and the From/Reply-To of
      the composed message itself; identity is Runtime-owned, and the
      Agent does *not* choose its sending identity.

   *  *draft.subject* and *draft.body_text* are REQUIRED and MAY be
      empty strings. body_text is *plain text*; this document defines no
      alternative body representation at this version.

   *  *draft.reply_to_message_id* (OPTIONAL, nullable) names the message
      this draft replies to, as an [RFC5322] message identifier.  It is
      composed directly into an In-Reply-To: header, which is why it
      carries a control-character pattern in the schema (below).

   *  *Recipient policy is a Runtime decision.* The Agent's chosen
      draft.to and draft.cc are *not* inherently trusted.  Allowlisting,
      task-counterpart binding, and any other recipient rule are
      evaluated Runtime-side.  A populated allowlist plus a fresh
      recipient is an exfiltration surface that the Runtime, not the
      Connector, must close.

   *  *Recipient syntax and header-injection discipline.* Each draft.to
      and draft.cc element is exactly one bare addr-spec: no display
      name, address list, quoted local part, comment, IP literal, or
      folding whitespace.  The schema pins the pattern.  This profile is
      deliberately narrower than [RFC5322], because those excluded forms
      are exactly what makes allowlist evaluation non-mechanical;
      internationalized (EAI/SMTPUTF8) addresses are out of scope at



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 24]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


      this version and may be added later.  A Runtime MUST reject — with
      a top-level rejected Result — a request whose recipient entries do
      not parse under this profile, MUST evaluate recipient policy over
      exactly the recipient set it will transmit to, and MUST NOT
      transmit to any address not present in draft.to or draft.cc.

      Separately, a Runtime MUST NOT allow any Agent-authored string —
      subject, a recipient entry, an attachment filename, an attachment
      media_type, draft.reply_to_message_id, in_reply_to, agent_id, ts,
      or body_text where it abuts headers — to introduce a header
      boundary in the composed message.  CR, LF, and NUL MUST be
      rejected or stripped before composition *even where schema
      validation was bypassed upstream*: the schema-level control-
      character patterns on subject, filename, media_type,
      reply_to_message_id, in_reply_to, agent_id, and ts are the first
      line of defense, not the only one.  Two of those fields matter for
      a reason worth stating explicitly, because narrower schema
      coverage in an earlier revision of this protocol missed exactly
      them: reply_to_message_id and media_type are composed _directly
      into headers_ — In-Reply-To: and a MIME part's Content-Type:
      [RFC2045] respectively — rather than into a body or a display
      field.

   *  *draft.attachments[]* (OPTIONAL) is an array of Descriptors, each
      carrying filename, media_type, size_bytes, and sha256. *size_bytes
      and sha256 are REQUIRED on every Descriptor*, computed by the
      Connector over the *decoded* bytes it wrote, with sha256 in
      lowercase hexadecimal.

      There is *no outbound content_ref*. The Runtime re-derives each
      Sidecar's path from req-<id> plus the Descriptor's array index,
      which is the sole binding authority; an Agent-supplied path string
      would be pure disagreement and attack surface, so it is absent
      from the schema entirely and additionalProperties: false rejects
      it. attachments: [] is valid and is equivalent to the member being
      absent; the Sidecar directory MUST then be absent.

      sha256 here is an integrity and deduplication aid, *not an
      outbound trust boundary*: the Agent controls both the bytes and
      the hash, so a mismatch catches corruption, never a hostile Agent.
      Its value to the Runtime is that it detects an inconsistent
      request, not that it authenticates one.

6.  Outbound: Result

   A Result is the Runtime's verdict for one consumed Submit Request,
   written to <volume-root>/<agent-id>/outbound/results/<id>.json.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 25]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "req_id": "00000001",
     "outcome": "accepted",
     "detail": null,
     "reason_code": "allowlisted",
     "ts": "2026-08-09T19:14:00Z",
     "recipients": ["owner@example.com"],
     "message_id": "<20260809191400.1@example.org>",
     "job_id": null,
     "attestation": {
       "form": "self-stamp",
       "token": "selfstamp.v1.abcdef",
       "claims": {
         "agent": "agent.research",
         "acts_for": "owner@example.com",
         "issued_at": "2026-08-09T19:14:00Z"
       }
     },
     "attachments": [
       { "index": 0, "outcome": "accepted", "detail": null }
     ]
   }

    Figure 3: draft/examples/result.json (illustrative — not a fixture)

   The normative shape is Appendix B.  The Result envelope is *open*: a
   consumer MUST tolerate members it does not recognize, at every level
   (Section 11.1).

6.1.  Field semantics and obligations

   *  *The Runtime writes exactly one Result per Submit Request it
      consumes.* A request the Runtime never consumes gets no Result,
      and no signal in this protocol distinguishes "not yet" from
      "never."

   *  *outcome* (REQUIRED) is one of accepted, queued_for_human, or
      rejected.  This is a *closed vocabulary*: it gates which
      processing path a document takes, so a consumer cannot safely
      treat an unrecognized value as opaque, and introducing a new value
      is a major change (Section 11.1).

   *  *Any policy miss — allowlist, rate limit, DLP hold, halt — MUST
      produce queued_for_human.* Never a silent send; never a silent
      drop.





Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 26]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *accepted* means the provider accepted the message for relay.
      Downstream delivery or quarantine is out of the Runtime's hands
      and is surfaced later via an inbound delivery-status notification,
      if any.

   *  *detail* (OPTIONAL, nullable) is human-readable text.  It carries
      no machine semantics.

   *  *reason_code* (OPTIONAL) records _which policy path_ authorized or
      refused the request; human text stays in detail.  A Runtime
      *SHOULD* set a reason on every Result, successes included.  The
      suggested vocabulary — recipient_bound, allowlisted,
      no_verified_counterparty, recipient_not_allowlisted, dlp_hold,
      no_screener, halted, rate_limited, unsupported_contract_version —
      is *extensible and not enum-locked in the schema*. Two consumer
      obligations follow: a consumer MUST tolerate a reason_code it does
      not recognize, treating it as opaque and never as an error, and a
      consumer MUST NOT infer the outcome from it. outcome is the sole
      authoritative verdict; reason_code only explains which path
      produced it, and a Runtime may add codes at any time without a
      protocol change. unsupported_contract_version is the code a
      Runtime sets on the rejected Result it writes for a version-
      refused Submit Request (Section 11.1).

   *  *ts* (OPTIONAL) is the Runtime-set, of-record time of the verdict,
      in ISO-8601 form.

   *  *recipients* (OPTIONAL) records the recipient set the Runtime
      actually transmitted to.

   *  *message_id* (OPTIONAL, nullable) is the [RFC5322] message
      identifier the Runtime assigned to the composed message.

   *  *job_id* (OPTIONAL, nullable) is a provider-side job identifier,
      opaque to this protocol.

   *  *attestation* (OPTIONAL) is the identity stamp the Runtime applied
      to the outbound message.  Its form is self-stamp or verifiable,
      distinguishing a stamp a stranger cannot verify from one that can
      be verified independently.  A Connector _surfaces_ an attestation;
      it never verifies one, which is a Runtime concern.

   *  *attachments[]* (OPTIONAL) carries one diagnostic entry per
      submitted attachment: index, an outcome of accepted, dlp_held,
      rejected_type, or too_large, and an optional detail. *index MUST
      equal the entry's own position in the array* — contiguous, unique,
      and covering 0 through n-1 exactly once.  Array position is the
      binding authority for attachments in both directions



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 27]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


      (Section 4.1).  This constraint is not expressible in JSON Schema
      and is enforced by the conformance gate as a named post-check
      rather than by the schema (Appendix H).

      *Two paths, never conflated.* A _malformed_ attachment — a size or
      digest mismatch, a missing or extra Sidecar, a duplicate index —
      is not a policy decision: it fails the whole request with a top-
      level rejected.  A _policy hold_ — DLP, a disallowed type, a size
      cap, including a fail-closed hold when no screener is available —
      is queued_for_human.  Per-attachment outcomes are diagnostic
      detail under *one* governing top-level outcome; they never license
      a partial send.

7.  Inbound: Deliver Notice and Inbound Message

   The Runtime writes one Deliver Notice per *delivered* message.
   Quarantined or unverified mail produces *no Notice*: it is logged
   Runtime-side and is never seen by the Agent.  The Notice is a
   _pointer and summary_; the body is fetched on demand from a separate
   spooled artifact (Section 7.3) and is *untrusted content*.































Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 28]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "notice_id": "1721457600000000000-4242",
     "ts": "2026-07-20T04:00:00Z",
     "kind": "deliver",
     "message": {
       "id": "42",
       "from": "Alex Doe <owner@example.com>",
       "subject": "status?",
       "preview": "hey, how is the run going",
       "mailbox": "inbox",
       "task_id": "0f1e2d3c4b5a6978",
       "thread_id": "T-9182",
       "in_reply_to": "<20260719120000.7@example.com>",
       "references": ["<20260718090000.3@example.com>"],
       "sender_standing": "known",
       "provenance": "external",
       "verdict": {
         "auth": "dmarc-pass",
         "screen": "clean",
         "entitlement": "task-counterparty"
       },
       "attachments": [
         {
           "filename": "invoice.pdf",
           "media_type": "application/pdf",
           "size_bytes": 12345,
           "disposition": "unscanned"
         }
       ]
     }
   }

      Figure 4: draft/examples/deliver-notice.json (illustrative — not
                                 a fixture)

   The normative shape is Appendix C.  The Deliver Notice envelope is
   *open*: a consumer MUST tolerate members it does not recognize, at
   every level (Section 11.1).

7.1.  Field semantics and obligations

   *The drop rule.* A Connector relays only deliver Notices.  It MUST
   drop — not surface — a Notice that fails *either* of two independent
   checks, treating a failure of either one alone as sufficient grounds
   to drop:





Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 29]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   1.  *Schema failure.* The Notice fails validation against the
       deliver-notice schema (Appendix C) for *any reason other than an
       unrecognized member*. That single formulation covers a kind other
       than deliver, a missing required member, an enum violation on a
       closed vocabulary, a pattern violation (including a traversal or
       character-set violation in notice_id, or a shape violation in
       content_ref's own pattern), a conditional (allOf / if-then)
       violation, and a type violation alike, with no need to enumerate
       schema-failure categories separately. *An unrecognized member is
       never grounds for a drop* (Section 11.1); that is the one carve-
       out from "fails schema validation."

   2.  *The content_ref index and prefix binding.* A Notice can pass
       check 1 — every member individually well-shaped — and still carry
       an attachment Descriptor whose content_ref does not equal
       <notice_id>.attachments/<i> for its own 0-based array position i
       (Section 7.2): a mismatched trailing index, or a leading
       notice_id prefix pointing into a _different_ Notice's Sidecar
       directory.  A Connector MUST run this check independently of
       schema validation and MUST drop the Notice on failure exactly as
       it would a schema failure.

   *This is not a closure over schema validation.* Check 2 binds two
   members of the same document — a Descriptor's content_ref against the
   enclosing document's own notice_id and against the Descriptor's own
   array position — against each other, which is not expressible in the
   JSON Schema vocabulary these schemas use [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12].  It
   therefore cannot be folded into "fails schema validation" no matter
   how the schema is phrased: it is a second, independent condition, not
   a special case of the first.  The conformance suite enforces it as a
   named post-check and pins it with a fixture that is schema-valid on
   its own and fails only this check (Appendix H).

   A *version refusal* — an absent or non-matching contract_version
   major — is explicitly *not* part of this drop path.  It is handled
   first and separately (Section 11.1) as a distinct, logged outcome: a
   Connector checks the version before it ever reaches schema
   validation, so a version-refused Notice never falls into the drop
   rule at all.

   A document with kind: "peer" found under inbound/notices/ fails check
   1 against this schema, and is dropped the same way (Appendix F, the
   peer-origin profile's cross-lock).

   *Field obligations.*






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 30]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *contract_version*, *notice_id*, *ts*, *kind*, and *message* are
      REQUIRED. notice_id is Runtime-minted and is pinned by the schema
      to a character set that is safe as a path component and as a
      content_ref prefix.

   *  Required members of message are id, from, subject, preview, and
      mailbox.  The rest is enrichment (Section 11.2).

   *  *message.id* is the provider's message identifier.  It is
      *external and not character-set-safe*, and MUST NOT be used as a
      path component anywhere (Section 4.1).

   *  *message.from is attacker-controlled display data.* Its display-
      name half is chosen freely by the sender —
      "security@yourbank.example <attacker@evil.example>" is a legal
      value — and it MUST NOT be used for any trust decision, nor
      rendered to a human or to an Agent as verified identity.  Verified
      sender identity is only ever what the Runtime summarizes into
      sender_standing and verdict; it is never the from string itself.

   *  *Presentation obligations.* A Connector that presents a message
      body to its Agent MUST convey two things, whatever words it uses:
      quoted or forwarded material inside the body carries no authority
      of its own — a message's authority extends to what its author
      wrote, never to what they relayed — and that an attachment's
      disposition is the Runtime's assertion about handling and not a
      scanner verdict, so a Connector MUST NOT imply that bytes have
      been screened and MUST NOT contradict the per-attachment status
      the Runtime published.  A Connector MUST also convey that an
      attachment's filename and media_type are sender-chosen display
      strings on the mail tree; on a tree whose sender the Runtime
      authenticated it SHOULD, and MUST where the attachment was relayed
      rather than authored by that sender.  On the mail tree a Connector
      MUST additionally convey that the sender is not authenticated
      beyond whatever standing the Runtime has already summarized —
      carried in sender_standing and verdict, named here as the locus
      and not as vocabulary to repeat to a reader — and that
      message.from is sender-chosen text.  These are obligations about
      substance, not vocabulary: a Connector satisfies them with any
      wording its reader can act on without consulting this document,
      and they MUST be satisfiable by a literal string the Connector
      carries, requiring no lookup or computation when a body is
      presented.








Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 31]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *The untrusted-content posture covers every sender-originated
      string* in the Notice and in the spooled Inbound Message:
      message.from, subject, preview, body_text, references, attachment
      filename and media_type, and the Inbound Message's from, to, cc,
      and subject.  This is not limited to the members called out
      individually here.

   *  *message.sender_standing* (OPTIONAL) is an *open, advisory
      vocabulary* — known, agent-tier, first-contact, read-only, and
      others.  How the values are computed is Runtime policy and out of
      scope; the wire fixes only today's known vocabulary, so that a
      Connector can tell its Agent "stranger," "agent," or "needs sign-
      off."  A Connector MUST tolerate a value outside this list,
      treating it as opaque — never as grounds to drop the Notice — and
      a Runtime MAY add a value as a minor change (Section 11.1).

   *  *message.provenance* (OPTIONAL) classifies the message source —
      external, internal, and others — so that a Runtime can route
      provenance-labelled screening.  It is advisory metadata, like
      verdict, and never a license for an Agent to obey body content.
      It is likewise an *open, advisory vocabulary*: a Connector MUST
      tolerate a value outside this list, treating it as opaque, and
      MUST NOT drop the Notice on its account; a Runtime MAY add a value
      as a minor change.

   *  *message.verdict* (OPTIONAL) carries the upstream authentication,
      screening, and entitlement results the Runtime consumed.  A
      Connector treats it as advisory metadata, never as license for an
      Agent to obey body content.  The object is open: unrecognized
      members inside it are tolerated, as they are everywhere else in
      this artifact.

   *  *message.thread_id*, *message.in_reply_to*, and
      *message.references* (all OPTIONAL) carry provider and [RFC5322]
      threading identity.  They grant correlation, never trust
      (Section 8).

   *  *message.task_id* (OPTIONAL) is Runtime-minted; Section 8 states
      the obligations on it.

   *Direction and openness.* This artifact is Runtime-authored, and its
   envelope is open at every level: a Connector MUST tolerate a member
   it does not recognize, in message or at the top level, and MUST NOT
   drop the Notice on that account.  Emitting an unrecognized member
   remains Runtime non-conformance (Section 11.1).






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 32]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


7.2.  Inbound attachment Descriptors

   *message.attachments[]* (OPTIONAL) is an array of Descriptors
   carrying filename, media_type, and size_bytes — all REQUIRED — plus a
   REQUIRED disposition, and OPTIONAL sha256 and content_ref members
   gated on it.

   *disposition is the Runtime's assertion, not a scanner verdict.* Its
   values are clean, stripped, quarantined, and unscanned, and the
   vocabulary is *closed*: it gates byte publication, so a new value
   would be a behavioral fork a consumer cannot treat as opaque, and
   introducing one is a major change (Section 11.1).  On what basis a
   Runtime asserts clean is deliberately unspecified — a screening
   pipeline's pass in one deployment, a closed operator-supervised
   topology in another.  That is Runtime policy and out of scope for the
   wire, the same posture sender_standing takes: the wire fixes the
   vocabulary, never the computation.  The Runtime is trusted by
   construction (Section 3.1); the load-bearing invariant is that the
   _Agent_ is not.

   The counterpart obligation is equally plain: *a Runtime that cannot
   make the determination MUST NOT assert clean.* It emits unscanned —
   or stripped or quarantined where it made that decision — and
   publishes no bytes.

   *Byte publication and the access grant.* A Runtime MAY publish an
   attachment's bytes at inbound/notices/<notice-id>.attachments/<index>
   *only* for a Descriptor it asserts disposition == "clean", and only
   then MAY it emit content_ref (a path of the form <notice-
   id>.attachments/<index>) and sha256.  Byte-absence remains the gate
   (Section 4.1) for anything not asserted clean.  Exposing sha256 on a
   withheld item would be a confirmation oracle for no integrity value,
   which is why it is clean-gated too.  Both conditionals are expressed
   in the schema.

   *The content_ref binding.* content_ref's leading notice_id prefix
   MUST equal the enclosing document's own notice_id, and its trailing
   <index> MUST equal the Descriptor's own 0-based array index.  The
   array index remains the sole binding authority (Section 4.1), and a
   consumer that resolves bytes MUST derive the path from the enclosing
   notice_id and the index — never trusting the content_ref string's own
   text as the path, since a Descriptor could otherwise point into
   another Notice's Sidecar directory.  This is a wire-shaped, document-
   level obligation, enforced by the conformance gate as a named post-
   check (Appendix H) in the same way the Result-side
   attachments[i].index == i binding is.





Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 33]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *A grant, never a directive.* A consumer MUST tolerate a Descriptor
   whose bytes it does not resolve — relaying the Notice as usual — and
   MUST NOT treat the presence of content_ref as a requirement to fetch.
   A Connector that never dereferences content_ref remains fully
   conformant.  A Connector MUST resolve published bytes only within its
   own Namespace's inbound/notices/ tree and MUST reject any content_ref
   that does not match the pinned pattern — the same confinement
   Section 4.1's read-side discipline requires generally.

   *filename and media_type here are attacker-controlled, untrusted
   display strings.* The untrusted-content posture extends to attachment
   Descriptors: a quarantined file named to look like an instruction is
   still an injection payload even with its bytes withheld.  A clean
   assertion covers the bytes' screening disposition, never the
   truthfulness of these strings.

   *Inbound size_bytes is provider-declared and therefore advisory and
   untrusted* — it comes from the provider's structure report, and is
   not Runtime-verified the way outbound size_bytes is.

   *MIME edges.* filename is the [RFC2047] / [RFC2231]-*decoded*,
   Runtime-sanitized display string.  An "attachment" is any part
   carrying Content-Disposition: attachment [RFC2183], or any named or
   non-inline text part — inline images and multipart/related parts
   count, which is the conservative reading of [RFC2045] and [RFC2046].
   The declared media_type is display-only: the Runtime sniffs the
   bytes, and the sniffed type governs policy on the outbound gate.

7.3.  The Inbound Message (body spool)

   The Runtime spools the delivered body at <volume-root>/<agent-
   id>/inbound/messages/notice-<id>.json, keyed on the Runtime-minted
   notice identifier — never on the provider message.id, for the same
   confirmed-exploit reason given in Section 4.1.

















Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 34]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "notice_id": "1721457600000000000-4242",
     "id": "42",
     "date": "Mon, 20 Jul 2026 04:00:00 +0000",
     "from": "Alex Doe <owner@example.com>",
     "to": "agent@example.org",
     "subject": "status?",
     "body_text": "hey, how is the run going",
     "attachments": [
       {
         "filename": "report.pdf",
         "media_type": "application/pdf",
         "size_bytes": 48213,
         "disposition": "unscanned"
       }
     ]
   }

     Figure 5: draft/examples/inbound-message.json (illustrative — not
                                 a fixture)

   The normative shape is Appendix D.  Required members are
   contract_version, notice_id, and body_text; the rest — id, date,
   from, to, cc, subject, and attachments[] — is enrichment
   (Section 11.2).  Descriptors here follow exactly the rules of
   Section 7.2, including the content_ref binding and the clean gating.
   This artifact's envelope is *open*, like the other Runtime-authored
   artifacts.

   *Resolution.* A Connector's read surface resolves a notice identifier
   to a body from this artifact only, never from a provider fetch.  The
   body is *untrusted content*, the same posture as the rest of message.

   *Enforcement by absence.* A body the Runtime withholds — because of
   screening or quarantine, or because the message was never delivered —
   is simply not spooled, and a read against a missing artifact returns
   "not resolved."  There is no other signal and no fallback fetch.  The
   same "not resolved" response also covers an artifact the Runtime
   later removes under its own retention policy (Section 4.2): from the
   Connector's side, retired and never-spooled are indistinguishable,
   and both are already-specified behavior.









Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 35]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


8.  Task Correlation

   The Runtime mints and owns task_id; a Connector only reads it, to
   correlate a Notice with prior work.  The minting and thread-
   resolution _algorithm_ is Runtime policy and out of scope.  This
   protocol fixes three security obligations on it.

   *  *task_id MUST be unguessable and Runtime-minted* — an HMAC over
      the thread root, for instance.  It MUST NOT be a sequential or
      otherwise guessable value, and it MUST NOT be a capability an
      inbound sender can assert. _(A guessable, sequential task_id was a
      confirmed exploit path in an early implementation.)_

   *  *Matching a task_id, by itself, MUST NOT grant a message entry
      into that task.* Authoritative correlation is header threading
      *plus* per-message verified sender identity.  A subaddress or
      header token supplied by an inbound sender is a _hint_ only, never
      authoritative: it is attacker-controllable, and it is stripped by
      many gateways.

   *  *Threading grants correlation, not trust.* A message that threads
      onto a known task is still identity-verified per message; it does
      not inherit the task's standing.

9.  Binding Record

   The Binding Record is written by the Runtime or provisioner at the
   *Volume root* — <volume-root>/identity.json, a sibling of <agent-
   id>/, not inside it — and names which mailbox this Volume is bound
   to.  Its normative shape is Appendix E.

   The Binding Record names which mailbox a Volume is bound to; it is
   informational and never consulted for enforcement (Section 9).

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "agent_id": "agent-research",
     "address": "agent@example.org",
     "provisioned_ts": "2026-07-20T04:10:56Z"
   }

                Figure 6: fixtures/valid/identity-basic.json









Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 36]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


9.1.  Field semantics and obligations

   *  *Informational, not authoritative.* The Volume is an Agent-
      writable filesystem, so a compromised Agent can edit or delete
      this file at will.  Attribution and policy stay keyed on Runtime-
      side configuration (Section 4.1).  This record grants nothing and
      is never consulted for enforcement.

   *  *Consumers MUST tolerate its absence*, and *MUST treat its
      contents as untrusted data*: a malformed, oversized, or hostile
      file MUST never crash a reader or otherwise affect protocol
      behavior.

   *  Its jobs are narrow by design: operator sanity — a human
      confirming which mailbox a Volume is bound to — a pre-start
      conflict check for whatever wrote it, catching for instance one
      Agent's credentials pointed at another Agent's Volume, and letting
      a Connector surface the Agent's own address back to its Agent.

   *  *The file is OPTIONAL* (Section 11.2): nothing in this protocol
      requires a Runtime to write it or a Connector to read it, and both
      sides MUST work correctly with it absent.

   *  Required members, if the file is present, are agent_id, address,
      and provisioned_ts. label is OPTIONAL. contract_version is
      OPTIONAL here — the one artifact where it is — because the file is
      not a protocol artifact a consumer must parse to function; if
      present it is pinned to "2".

   *  This artifact's envelope is *closed* (additionalProperties:
      false), for a different reason than the Submit Request's is:
      closure here is an anti-secret-leak lint, catching a provisioner
      that writes credential material into a file living on an Agent-
      readable Volume.  It is not a compatibility surface.

10.  The Peer Directory

   A Runtime MAY publish, at the Agent's Namespace root (<agent-
   id>/directory.json, beside the lanes rather than inside one), a per-
   instance projection of the authorisation graph naming which peers
   that Agent may address.










Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 37]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "router": "amap.router@fleet.example",
     "written_at": "2026-09-18T12:00:00Z",
     "delegate_to": [
       "bravo@fleet.example",
       "charlie@fleet.example"
     ],
     "mail_to": []
   }

       Figure 7: draft/examples/directory.json (illustrative — not a
                                  fixture)

   *  *Advisory, never authoritative.* The directory is the Runtime's
      most recent word about the graph, and grants nothing.  A Connector
      MUST NOT treat an address's presence as a prediction that a
      submission to it will be accepted, nor its absence as a prediction
      of refusal: authorisation is evaluated by the Runtime at
      submission time, and the Result (Section 6) is the only thing that
      reports what happened.  A consumer that reads the directory as a
      prediction is wrong even when the file is current.

   *  *A Runtime MUST NOT read directory.json back, for any purpose.* It
      is write-only from the Runtime's side: the graph is derived from
      policy, the file is a projection of the graph, and nothing derives
      the graph from the file.  Enforcement remains the Runtime's own
      check against its graph, on every message.  The prohibition is on
      the direction rather than the purpose, because the ways this
      decays — as an optimisation, a cache, a recovery source, or a
      cross-check — all have innocent intent, and the last two turn a
      projection into a source.  A projection that can be read back
      becomes a cache; a cache becomes a record; a record that disagrees
      with policy wins by accident.

   *  *Per-instance projection.* Each Agent's directory carries only the
      edges that Agent is party to.  It MUST NOT carry the set of peers
      who may address that Agent, which is an allowlist in all but name,
      and MUST NOT carry the Agent's own address — attribution is the
      Namespace a file arrived in (Section 4), so an address an Agent
      reads is a claim rather than an identity.

   *  router is the publishing Runtime's own address and MUST NOT appear
      in either list.  Every address is one bare addr-spec (Section 5).

   *  *Both lists are always present*, and empty when that lane is
      closed for this Agent; mail_to is empty in a delegation-only
      deployment.  Absent and empty MUST NOT be conflated.



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 38]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *Written whole and atomically.* A Runtime MUST NOT publish a newly
      adopted instance's address to others before it has adopted that
      instance itself.

   *  *A Runtime that publishes the directory MUST ensure the Agent can
      read it*, and SHOULD expose it read-only.  Publishing to a path
      the Agent's Namespace does not expose is not conformant: the write
      succeeds, the file is correct, and no Agent can read it — a
      failure that reports nothing on either side.  Publishing is
      optional, so a Runtime that cannot make the file readable MUST NOT
      publish it; an unreadable directory is indistinguishable from an
      absent one to a consumer, and worse than an absent one to an
      operator, who has a file on disk that looks like it is working.
      The trap follows from the location: the file deliberately belongs
      to no lane, which is what keeps a delegation-only deployment from
      materialising a mail tree, and is exactly what places it outside
      an exposure built lane by lane.

   *  *written_at* is the only staleness signal a consumer gets: an
      honest marker, not a freshness guarantee.

   *  *Where the consumer is an Agent rather than a parser, these become
      obligations to convey.* A Connector that surfaces the directory to
      its Agent instead of interpreting it satisfies the obligations
      above by stating them, under the presentation rule in Section 7:
      the Agent is the party forming a belief, so the Connector MUST
      convey that an address's presence is not a prediction of
      acceptance, that the file may be absent, that an empty list and an
      absent list differ, and that written_at is the only staleness
      signal there is.  A Connector with no directory parser does not
      thereby satisfy them vacuously.

   *  *The file MAY be absent* — before first adoption, on a Runtime
      that does not implement this section, or after a failed write —
      and a consumer MUST tolerate absence exactly as it tolerates a
      missing Binding Record (Section 9).

   *  *A Runtime that cannot write it keeps routing.* The directory is
      advisory, so a failed write loses a convenience, not the ability
      to enforce; failing closed would convert an advisory artifact into
      a dependency.  The Runtime MUST log the failure.  The Agent's only
      signal remains written_at going stale.

11.  Versioning and Conformance







Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 39]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


11.1.  Versioning

   *The fail-closed rule.* contract_version is a major-version string.
   A consumer that reads a *higher major* than it speaks MUST *fail
   closed* — refuse to process the artifact — and MUST NOT silently mis-
   parse it.

   *Version-check ordering.* A consumer MUST implement the version check
   by reading contract_version *before* any schema validation, comparing
   majors as non-negative decimal integers.  An absent major, a lower
   major, or a higher major is a *version refusal*: fail closed, as a
   distinct, logged outcome, never folded into the malformed-document
   drop path of Section 7.1.

   Checking the version first is what makes fail-closed implementable at
   all.  A validator that runs schema checks first cannot distinguish
   "wrong version" from "malformed," and a strict schema would reject a
   future-major document for the wrong reason entirely.

   This ordering rule is about _inbound_ artifacts a Connector consumes,
   which have no mechanism in this protocol to carry a distinct outcome
   back to the Runtime.  It does not reach the _outbound_ direction: a
   Runtime version-refusing a Submit Request MAY carry that refusal on
   the ordinary request-rejection path — a top-level rejected Result
   with reason_code: "unsupported_contract_version" (Section 6.1) — and,
   per the conformance classes below, MUST do so for the version-absent
   request fixture.  That is still a distinct, legible outcome rather
   than a fold into the malformed-request case: reason_code is exactly
   this protocol's mechanism for saying _why_ a rejected fired, and a
   consumer MUST already tolerate a reason_code it does not otherwise
   interpret.  A Runtime has no equivalent document to write for a
   version-refused _Notice_ it never emits — hence the asymmetry:
   logged-only inbound, rejected outbound.


















Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 40]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *Why a version signal, rather than unknown-member rejection, is the
   boundary.* At the transition from wire major "1" to "2", when
   attachment support was added, every top-level schema and every nested
   object except verdict and attestation.claims was
   additionalProperties: false.  Under that regime, adding a member is
   not a safe additive change the way it would be under a permissive
   envelope: a strict major-1 validator rejects the *whole document*,
   not just the new member.  Inbound, that is *silent total message
   loss* — an attachment-bearing email vanishes instead of degrading.
   Outbound, it is an accidental schema error rather than a designed
   refusal.  And there is no signal to gate on while contract_version
   stays "1", because the new member is invisible to anything that would
   need to react to it.  That is why attachments required a *major*
   bump: a major-1 consumer receiving a "2" document hits fail-closed
   _by version_, a legible and designed refusal, and both sides upgrade
   deliberately.

   Explicitly deleted from this protocol's reasoning: any framing in
   which additionalProperties: false rejection *is* the version
   boundary.  That conflates two different axes — schema strictness and
   protocol version — and produces catastrophic behavior (whole-document
   loss) exactly where a version check should produce a legible refusal.

   *Unknown-member tolerance is direction-aware.* This is the rule that
   repairs the versioning model, and it is stated per direction because
   the two directions have opposite threat models.

   *  *Runtime-authored artifacts — Deliver Notice, Inbound Message,
      Result — are open.* A consumer MUST ignore members it does not
      recognize, at every level of the document, and MUST NOT reject,
      drop, or fail the artifact on their account.  Strictness on this
      direction defended nothing: the producer is trusted by
      construction, and in the one posture where an attacker can author
      a Notice — a writable inbound tree — that attacker can author a
      fully schema-valid one, so strictness was never the defense there.
      Its failure mode was silent mail loss.  Emitting an unknown member
      remains a *producer* non-conformance: a Runtime MUST NOT emit
      members undefined at the version it claims.  In the schemas,
      additionalProperties: false is absent from the deliver-notice,
      inbound-message, and result schemas at every level — top level,
      message, Descriptor items, and attestation — while the clean-
      gating conditionals are orthogonal and remain.









Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 41]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *The Submit Request envelope stays closed*, additionalProperties:
      false at every level.  Closure is doing real security work there:
      it is what bars an outbound content_ref and any other smuggled
      member; the validator is the trusted Runtime; and a refusal is a
      _legible, per-request_ rejected Result, never a silent loss.  A
      Runtime MUST reject a request carrying unrecognized members.

   *  *Consequently:* adding an optional member to a Runtime-authored
      artifact is genuinely additive and is a minor change; adding any
      member to the Submit Request is a major change.

   *  The Binding Record is unchanged on this axis and stays closed for
      the separate reason given in Section 9.1.

   *Tolerance extends to values, not only members.* An optional,
   explicitly advisory enum on a Runtime-authored artifact —
   message.sender_standing and message.provenance (Section 7.1) — is
   scoped the same way.  A consumer MUST tolerate a value it does not
   recognize, treating it as opaque or as the member being absent, and
   MUST NOT reject, drop, or fail the artifact on that account; a
   Runtime MAY add a value to either vocabulary as a minor change.  This
   closes the same failure mode one indirection over: without it, a
   Runtime adding a fifth sender_standing or a third provenance value
   would silently lose every Notice carrying it, against every Connector
   still validating the old enum — identical to the member case, just at
   the value level.  In the schemas, the enum constraint is absent from
   these two members.

   This is *not* a universal loosening of every enum. kind, outcome —
   both the top-level Result outcome and the per-attachment outcome —
   and the inbound Descriptor's disposition remain *closed, enum-locked
   vocabularies*. kind and outcome gate which processing path a document
   takes at all, and disposition gates byte publication (Section 7.2),
   so a new value in any of them is a behavioral fork a consumer cannot
   safely treat as opaque.  Introducing one is a major change.

   *Two version axes, allowed to diverge.* The *wire major* tracks
   whole-document acceptance compatibility.  The *document version*
   tracks the fuller set of obligations, including narrower, disclosed
   producer-side tightenings that do not rise to that level.  Document
   version 3.0.0 is a major document bump — it moves fixtures between
   the valid and invalid sets, and it adds Runtime obligations a
   strictly-compliant earlier implementation does not meet — while the
   wire major stays "2".

   Document version 3.1.0 (DRAFT) is an additive *minor* bump over
   3.0.0; the wire major stays "2".  It introduces the outbound
   extension space and its one normative clarification (Section 4.1,



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 42]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   Section 12.15), and the peer-origin profile's schema and conformance
   fixtures (Appendix F, Appendix H).  No existing schema rule or
   fixture changed.  The profile's prose is a companion document not yet
   drafted; until it is, the schema and the peer-* fixtures are
   normative for the shape of a peer notice, and this document specifies
   nothing about the peer/ tree beyond that shape.

   The reasoning for holding the wire major is worth stating, because
   the alternative is tempting and wrong.  The wire major exists to
   force a legible fail-closed refusal when a _whole document_ that a
   counterpart already accepts would otherwise be silently misread or
   silently dropped — the catastrophic, undetectable failure mode a
   version bump exists to convert into a designed refusal.  Document
   version 3.0.0 does *not* claim that producer bytes are unchanged;
   they are not, on both sides (see the change log).  But neither
   narrowing is that failure mode: each travels a designed, legible,
   per-artifact refusal path this protocol has always sanctioned, rather
   than a whole-document rejection triggered by an unrelated member.
   The Submit Request tightening yields a per-request rejected Result;
   the notice_id character-set tightening yields a per-Notice Connector-
   side drop under check 1 of Section 7.1 — a real cost, disclosed in
   the change log, but a narrow and legible one, not silent total loss.
   Bumping the wire major to "3" would instead force every major-2
   counterpart on *both* sides to refuse *all* traffic outright,
   including all the traffic the tolerance rule newly protects —
   inflicting exactly the catastrophic, undisclosed mail loss this
   version exists to repair, in order to fix incompatibilities that
   already have narrower, disclosed failure paths.

   *Corrections.* Two claims that shipped in earlier revisions of this
   protocol's normative text were false, and are named here rather than
   quietly replaced, because an implementer who read them may have built
   against them.

   1.  *The write-rule "strengthening" that was a regression.* An
       earlier revision described the exclusive-create and no-symlink-
       follow requirement on the final path component as having been
       "strengthened to" the pinned directory-descriptor walk — that is,
       replaced by it — and deleted the earlier clause outright.  That
       was a *weakening*, not a strengthening: a parent chain pinned by
       descriptor is silent about the final .tmp filename itself, so
       dropping exclusive-create there let an Agent that pre-plants a
       symlink at a predictable .tmp name have the Runtime write through
       it.  Section 4.1 now states the rule conjunctively, with all
       three legs required together.






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 43]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   2.  *The drop rule described as a closure over schema validation.* An
       earlier revision described the inbound drop rule as a pure
       closure over schema validation, and claimed that formulation was
       exact against the fixture set.  Both statements were false: the
       content_ref index and prefix binding is not expressible in the
       schema dialect used here, and a fixture exists that is schema-
       valid on its own and must nonetheless be dropped.  Section 7.1
       now states two independent checks, and so does the Connector
       conformance class below.

   A third correction concerns this protocol's own change history rather
   than an obligation, and is recorded in the change log: the document
   version that introduced message.provenance was labelled an additive
   minor change, which was unsound against the strictly-validating
   consumers of the time.  The change log states what actually happened
   rather than relabelling the history.

   *Change control.* A capability change starts with a change to this
   document, its schemas, and its fixtures, _before_ either side
   implements it.  Neither a Runtime nor a Connector may invent a wire
   member locally.  Additive and backward-compatible changes are minor
   bumps; any change that breaks an existing fixture is a major bump,
   taken deliberately by both sides.

11.2.  Required versus optional

   contract_version is REQUIRED on every protocol artifact — Submit
   Request, Deliver Notice, and Result — with the Binding Record as the
   single exception (Section 9.1).  The rest of this table reflects what
   implementations emit today; specified-but-unbuilt enrichment stays
   optional, and tightening any of it to required would be a future
   major bump.

   +===================+===================+==========================+
   | Artifact          | Required          | Optional (specified; may |
   |                   |                   | be absent)               |
   +===================+===================+==========================+
   | *deliver-notice*  | contract_version, | message.{task_id,        |
   |                   | notice_id, ts,    | thread_id, in_reply_to,  |
