   inbound/notices/processed/ is an OPTIONAL *directory convention*
   (Section 4.1), not a protocol artifact: it carries no schema, and no
   fixture exists or is needed for it.

   Emission of contract_version on the three protocol artifacts is
   mandatory.  An implementation not yet emitting it has an
   implementation conformance gap, not a license from this document.






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 45]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


11.3.  Conformance

   *The fixtures are the other side.* fixtures/ holds golden artifacts,
   and a producer or consumer proves conformance by passing them with
   *no counterpart present* (Appendix H).  That is what makes
   independent implementation practical: neither side needs the other to
   exist in order to demonstrate conformance.

   Not every obligation in this document is wire-shaped.  A _behavioral_
   obligation — one about how an implementation acts against a
   filesystem, rather than about the shape of a document — lies outside
   the fixture gate by construction and is checked operationally
   instead.  Appendix H lists every obligation of this kind that a green
   run does not prove.

   This document defines two conformance classes.  An implementation MAY
   claim both.  Claiming either without the corresponding fixture run,
   and without the prescribed operational check for that class's
   behavioral obligations, is not conformance.

   *Runtime conformance class.* An implementation claiming Runtime
   conformance:

   *  MUST produce Deliver Notice documents valid against the deliver-
      notice schema (Appendix C) and Result documents valid against the
      result schema (Appendix B); MAY produce Inbound Message documents,
      which when produced MUST be valid against the inbound-message
      schema (Appendix D); and MAY produce a Binding Record valid
      against the binding-record schema (Appendix E).

   *  MUST consume Submit Request documents: it MUST accept every valid
      request-* fixture and MUST reject every invalid request-* fixture.

   *  MUST demonstrate its producing side by confirming that its own
      emitted Notices, Results, and Inbound Messages satisfy the same
      schemas the suite's valid notice-*, result-*, and message-*
      fixtures satisfy — *including the three fixtures carrying
      unrecognized members*. A Runtime MUST NOT itself emit unrecognized
      members, but its _parser_, exercised by those fixtures, is what a
      Connector conformance run depends on it never having to special-
      case.  It MUST also confirm that any Binding Record it writes
      satisfies the valid identity-* shape.

   *  MUST uphold the filesystem and policy obligations of Sections 4
      through 8 that no document validator can observe.  Appendix H
      lists them explicitly as what a green fixture run does *not*
      prove, and they are obligations of the class regardless — write-
      side path discipline (the conjunctive parent-chain-pinning, no-



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 46]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


      follow-while-building, and non-following-final-component rule),
      ingest by copy, read-side open discipline, and single-writer/
      single-drainer chief among them.

   *Connector conformance class.* An implementation claiming Connector
   conformance:

   *  MUST produce Submit Request documents valid against the submit-
      request schema (Appendix A), and MUST NOT emit an outbound
      content_ref (Section 5.1).

   *  MUST consume Deliver Notice, Inbound Message, and Result
      documents: it MUST accept every valid notice-*, message-*, and
      result-* fixture — *including those carrying unrecognized members
      or unrecognized advisory-enum values* — and MUST reject, meaning
      drop rather than surface, every invalid notice-* fixture *except
      the version-refusal one*, which it MUST instead refuse via the
      distinct version-refusal path (Section 11.1): never folded into
      the drop path, and never surfaced to the Agent either.

      Section 7.1's drop rule is *two independent conditions, not a
      closure over schema validation*. "Fails schema validation for any
      reason other than an unrecognized member" (check 1) covers ten of
      the eleven other invalid notice-* fixtures — missing-required-
      member, wrong-kind, enum, pattern, and conditional violations
      alike.  The eleventh is schema-valid on its own, producing zero
      errors from the gate's schema validator, and is caught only by the
      content_ref index and prefix binding (check 2, Section 7.2), a
      named post-check the schema cannot express.  A Connector
      conformance claim requires running *both* checks; schema
      validation alone does not close this set.

      Accepting the clean-Descriptor fixture — a Descriptor asserted
      clean and carrying content_ref and sha256 — is part of this
      obligation, and acceptance means relaying the Notice, not fetching
      the bytes: a Connector that never dereferences content_ref
      satisfies it (Section 7.2).

   *  MUST return "not resolved" for a body whose Inbound Message is
      absent, and MUST NOT attempt any fallback fetch (Section 7.3).

   *  MUST tolerate a Binding Record that is absent, and MUST NOT crash
      or otherwise misbehave on one that is hostile or malformed
      (Section 9.1).

   *  MUST NOT require write access anywhere under inbound/,
      demonstrated by the operational check below rather than by a
      fixture (Section 4.1).



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 47]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  MUST demonstrate its producing side by confirming that its own
      emitted requests satisfy the same schema the suite's valid
      request-* fixtures satisfy, and MUST uphold the write-ordering,
      atomicity, and read-discipline obligations of Section 4.1, which
      the fixtures cannot check.

   *Read-only inbound tolerance — the prescribed operational check.* Run
   the Connector against an inbound tree it cannot write — a genuinely
   read-only mount, not merely cleared permission bits, since a same-uid
   Agent can change a mode it owns — and confirm that it starts, relays
   every pending Notice, resolves bodies, and submits outbound requests,
   without requiring any write under inbound/ to succeed.

12.  Security Considerations

   This section gathers the threats this protocol's obligations exist to
   address.  It introduces no new mechanism: every requirement
   referenced here is stated normatively in Sections 4 through 11.  The
   organizing principle throughout is the invariant of Section 3.2 —
   enforcement is Runtime-side, and no property depends on the Agent or
   its Connector behaving.

   The threat actor assumed throughout is a *fully compromised Agent*
   with write access to its own Namespace, running as a uid that owns
   the files it creates, able to act concurrently with the Runtime, and
   able to observe or predict the filenames the Runtime is about to use.

12.1.  Path authority and traversal

   An identifier drawn from a file's _contents_ MUST NOT name a write
   path (Section 4.1).  An early implementation trusted a req_id member
   inside a request body to name the path its Result would be written
   to, which is a confirmed exploit: the Agent controls that member and
   could therefore direct a Runtime-privileged write anywhere the
   Runtime could reach.  The obligation is that the Runtime derives
   identifiers from the _validated filename_, over a restricted
   character set, and re-derives every path from data it controls.

   The same reasoning is why inbound Sidecar directories and the body
   spool are keyed on the Runtime-minted notice identifier rather than
   the provider message.id: the provider identifier is external,
   arbitrary, and not character-set-safe, and using one as a path
   component was itself a confirmed exploit path.  The schemas pin
   notice_id and req_id to character sets that are safe as path
   components; message.id is deliberately unconstrained, because it is
   never used as one.





Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 48]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


12.2.  Symlinks, descriptors, and open discipline

   A shared filesystem between a trusted and an untrusted party makes
   every path-based check racy.  The Agent can replace any component of
   a path it owns with a symlink, at any moment, including between a
   Runtime's check and the Runtime's subsequent act.

   Section 4.1 states the write-side discipline as three conjunctive
   requirements, and the conjunction is the point: each leg closes a gap
   the other two leave open.

   *  Pinning only the final component leaves the _parent_ swappable,
      and rename and directory-creation calls have no no-follow flag at
      all — so a bare "do not follow symlinks on writes" rule is not
      sufficient.

   *  Pinning the parent chain without refusing symlinks _while
      acquiring_ it means the pinned descriptor may point at whatever
      the Agent planted before the Runtime opened it — including across
      a Runtime restart, when the chain is re-opened.

   *  Pinning the whole chain correctly still says nothing about the
      final filename.  Every Runtime-written filename in the layout tree
      is predictable or observable to the Agent, so a pre-planted
      symlink at that name receives the Runtime's write with the
      Runtime's privileges unless the final open refuses to follow it
      and, where the file is newly created, refuses to reuse an existing
      name at all (O_EXCL).

   The append-only audit log is the one write with no .tmp sibling to
   lean on, and it is called out separately for two reasons.  O_EXCL
   cannot apply to a file that legitimately already exists, so the
   final-component protection there is a no-follow, append-mode, *non-
   blocking* open plus an fstat through the resulting descriptor.  The
   non-blocking part is load-bearing rather than a performance nicety: a
   no-follow flag does not apply to a FIFO, because a FIFO is not a
   symlink, and opening a FIFO for writing blocks until a reader
   appears.  An Agent that plants a FIFO at that filename therefore
   stalls the Runtime's drain indefinitely — a denial of service that
   the exclusive-create branch happens to refuse for free, and that this
   branch must refuse explicitly.










Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 49]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   The read side mirrors all of it (Section 4.1): per-component no-
   follow opens or an equivalently pinned walk, a non-blocking open, an
   fstat through the open descriptor rather than a pre-open stat (which
   is itself a race), refusal of a multiply-linked file, and enforced
   size and count caps.  The caps are not optional hardening: the
   too_large Result value presumes one, and without them an Agent can
   present an unbounded Sidecar or an unbounded request and exhaust the
   Runtime.

12.3.  Time-of-check to time-of-use, and ingest by copy

   Even with every open performed correctly, validating a file _in
   place_ and then using it is a race: the Agent can rewrite the bytes
   between the check and the use, so the document that passed policy is
   not necessarily the document that gets composed and sent.  The
   obligation that closes this is ingest by copy (Section 4.1) — the
   Runtime copies the request and every Sidecar into Runtime-private
   Staging outside the Volume, and validates, evaluates policy on, and
   composes exclusively from that private copy, never re-reading an
   Agent-writable path after a decision that depends on its content.

   This is also what keeps the trust model honest.  Without it, the
   property "the request the Runtime approved is the request the Runtime
   sent" would rest on the Connector not rewriting a published file — an
   Agent-side obligation carrying a Runtime-side safety property, which
   the invariant of Section 3.2 forbids.  With it, that Connector
   obligation is pure well-formedness: a Runtime MAY treat an observed
   post-publish change as malformed, but nothing depends on the
   Connector honoring it.

12.4.  Concurrency

   Every atomicity guarantee in this protocol — the .tmp-then-rename
   discipline, the commit sentinel, the derivation of req_id from the
   maximum of the pending, processed, and result sets — assumes a single
   writer and a single drainer per Namespace, and none of them provides
   mutual exclusion (Section 4.1).  Two concurrent drains can deliver
   the same request twice; two concurrent writers can collide on a
   req_id and clobber a published request, producing a verdict that
   names a request that no longer exists as written.  The exclusion
   mechanism lives outside this protocol, and an implementation that
   does not provide one is not conformant, because behavior under
   violation is unspecified rather than merely degraded.








Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 50]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


12.5.  Attribution spoofing

   Attribution is the Namespace a file arrived in, never an identifier
   inside the file (Section 4.1).  A compromised Agent can write any
   agent_id it likes into a request; the member exists only as a cross-
   check, and a Runtime MUST reject a mismatch rather than believe it.
   Structural isolation is what actually enforces this: a Connector
   scoped to its own Namespace cannot name another Agent's.

   The Binding Record deserves the same skepticism from the other
   direction (Section 9.1).  It sits on an Agent-writable Volume, so its
   contents are untrusted data, it grants nothing, and it is never
   consulted for enforcement.

12.6.  Untrusted content

   Inbound mail is an injection vector aimed at the Agent's reasoning,
   and this protocol's posture is that _every sender-originated string_
   is untrusted content: bodies, subjects, previews, threading
   references, sender display names, and attachment Descriptors alike
   (Section 7.1).

   Two cases are worth restating because they are the ones most often
   assumed safe.

   *message.from is attacker-controlled display data.* Its display-name
   half is chosen freely by the sender, so a value such as
   "security@yourbank.example <attacker@evil.example>" is entirely legal
   and renders convincingly.  It MUST NOT be used for a trust decision
   or shown to a human or an Agent as verified identity.  Verified
   sender identity is only ever what the Runtime summarizes into
   sender_standing and verdict.

   *An attachment filename is an injection payload.* A Descriptor is
   metadata about a file the Agent may never receive the bytes of, and a
   clean Disposition asserts something about _bytes_, never about the
   truthfulness of the strings describing them.  A quarantined file
   named to look like an instruction reaches the Agent's context intact
   even though its bytes were withheld. media_type is likewise a
   declaration, which is why policy is governed by the Runtime's own
   sniffing of the bytes rather than by the declared type.

   verdict, sender_standing, and provenance are advisory metadata for
   routing and presentation.  None of them is a license for an Agent to
   obey body content, and this document deliberately does not define
   what an Agent should do with a message — that is Connector and
   deployment policy.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 51]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


12.7.  Recipient policy and header injection

   Recipient policy is the exfiltration boundary, and it is a Runtime
   decision (Section 5.1).  The Agent's draft.to and draft.cc are
   requests, not instructions.  Two obligations make the boundary
   mechanical rather than best-effort: the Runtime MUST evaluate policy
   over exactly the recipient set it will transmit to, and it MUST NOT
   transmit to any address not present in those members.  Without the
   first, policy can be evaluated over a parse of the recipients that
   differs from the one used for transmission; without the second, a
   Runtime-side addition (a bcc, an archive address) escapes the
   evaluated set.

   The narrow addr-spec profile exists to make the evaluation
   mechanical.  Display names, address lists inside a single element,
   quoted local parts, comments, IP literals, and folding whitespace are
   precisely the forms that make "does this address match the allowlist"
   a parsing problem with divergent answers — the classic confusion in
   which one parser sees the allowlisted address and the transmitting
   parser sees the attacker's.  The profile is deliberately narrower
   than [RFC5322] for that reason, and the cost is disclosed: some
   legitimate [RFC5322] addresses cannot be expressed at this version.

   Header injection is the second half.  Any Agent-authored string that
   reaches the composed message can attempt to introduce a header
   boundary with CR, LF, or NUL.  The schema patterns are the first line
   of defense, but a Runtime MUST also reject or strip those characters
   at composition time, because a document can reach composition by a
   path where schema validation was bypassed upstream.  The two fields
   most easily overlooked are the ones composed _directly into headers_
   rather than into a body or display context: reply_to_message_id,
   which becomes an In-Reply-To: header, and an attachment's media_type,
   which becomes a MIME part's Content-Type: [RFC2045].  An earlier
   revision's schema coverage stopped at subject and filename and missed
   exactly these.

12.8.  The outbound digest is not a trust boundary

   sha256 on an outbound attachment Descriptor is computed by the
   Connector over bytes the Connector wrote (Section 5.1).  The Agent
   controls both, so a matching digest proves only that the request is
   internally consistent.  It catches corruption and interrupted writes;
   it authenticates nothing.  A Runtime MUST NOT treat a digest match as
   evidence about the content's safety, and MUST apply its own policy —
   sniffing the bytes, applying type and size rules — to the staged copy
   regardless.





Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 52]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   The inbound direction is weaker still and is labelled as such:
   inbound size_bytes is provider-declared and advisory, not Runtime-
   verified (Section 7.2).

12.9.  Confirmation-oracle avoidance

   Inbound metadata is gated so that withholding bytes does not become
   an information channel. sha256 on an inbound Descriptor is emitted
   only where the Runtime asserts clean (Section 7.2).  Publishing a
   digest for a withheld attachment would let an Agent confirm whether a
   _guessed_ file was the one quarantined — a confirmation oracle —
   while providing no integrity value at all, since the Agent has no
   bytes to check it against.

   The same principle governs quarantined mail generally: it produces no
   Notice at all, rather than a Notice announcing that something was
   withheld.

12.10.  Byte-absence and artifact-absence as the access gate

   The access gate in this protocol is the absence of bytes, not a flag
   inside a document (Section 4.1).  A Runtime MUST NOT place non-clean
   bytes in an Agent's Namespace; content_ref is the grant, and it
   exists only where bytes were published.  An Agent that ignores every
   Disposition it is shown still cannot read what was never written.

   The same shape appears for bodies: a withheld or never-delivered
   message is simply not spooled, and a read against a missing artifact
   returns "not resolved," with no fallback fetch available to the
   Connector (Section 7.3).  Because retention may also remove an
   artifact (Section 4.2), "retired" and "never spooled" are
   indistinguishable from the Connector's side — which is a deliberate
   property, not an ambiguity to be resolved by a new signal.

   The content_ref binding rules (Section 7.2) close the corresponding
   path-confusion risk: a consumer derives the byte path from the
   enclosing notice_id and the array index rather than from the
   content_ref string, and refuses any reference that does not match the
   pinned pattern or points outside its own inbound tree.  Otherwise a
   Descriptor could name another Notice's Sidecar directory — including
   one belonging to a different delivery whose bytes the Agent was never
   granted.









Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 53]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


12.11.  Fail-closed version handling, and the cost of tolerance

   A consumer reading a higher major than it speaks fails closed, and
   the version check runs _before_ schema validation so that "wrong
   version" and "malformed" remain distinguishable (Section 11.1).
   Folding the two together is how a protocol acquires silent,
   undiagnosable mail loss.

   The unknown-member tolerance rule is direction-aware precisely
   because tolerance has a security cost in one direction and a safety
   benefit in the other.  On Runtime-authored artifacts, strictness
   defended nothing — the producer is trusted, and an attacker able to
   author a Notice at all (a writable inbound tree) can author a schema-
   valid one — while its failure mode was silent mail loss.  On the
   Agent-authored Submit Request, closure is doing real work: it is what
   makes an outbound content_ref, or any other smuggled member, a hard
   rejection rather than a member the Runtime might one day interpret.
   A Runtime therefore MUST keep rejecting unrecognized members inbound
   from an Agent, and its rejection is legible — a rejected Result —
   rather than silent.

   The value-level tolerance is scoped to the two explicitly advisory
   vocabularies for the same reason: kind, outcome, and disposition gate
   processing paths and byte publication, and treating an unrecognized
   value in any of them as opaque would let a producer's new value
   silently select a consumer's default path.

12.12.  Inbound integrity and the writability of the inbound tree

   A read-only inbound mount is the mechanism that makes a delivered
   Notice unforgeable (Section 4.1).  Permission bits alone do not
   achieve it: a same-uid Agent can change a mode it owns, so an inbound
   tree protected only by bits is writable by the attacker in practice.
   Deployments that leave inbound writable should understand what they
   are accepting — an Agent can then author a schema-valid Notice for
   mail that never arrived, or alter one that did.

   This is also why the tolerance rule does not weaken the inbound
   direction: in the writable-inbound posture, the attacker's forgery is
   schema-valid anyway, so schema strictness was never the control.  The
   control is the mount.

   Correspondingly, a Connector MUST NOT require write access under
   inbound/, and consumption tracking is Connector-private state kept
   elsewhere (Section 4.1).  A Connector that crashes on a read-only
   inbound tree is broken against any Runtime enforcing inbound
   integrity.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 54]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


12.13.  Retention, deletion, and lost verdicts

   Deletion rights are named per artifact class (Section 4.2) because an
   unnamed right becomes either unbounded growth or an accidental data-
   loss path.  Two hazards are worth restating.

   *A Result deleted before it is read is a lost verdict.* No signal in
   this protocol tells a Runtime that a Connector has read one, so
   Runtime-side retention SHOULD be age-based and generous.

   *Deletion interacts with req_id monotonicity.* A Connector exercising
   its deletion rights in processed/ or results/ removes exactly the
   state from which the next req_id is derived, and MUST preserve
   monotonicity by other durable means.  Symmetrically, a Runtime MUST
   NOT treat processed/ as durable state — for deduplication, for
   instance — because the Connector may delete there.  The Runtime's own
   record of what it sent belongs outside this protocol entirely.

12.14.  What is wire-verifiable, and what is a Runtime obligation

   A green conformance run proves that documents have the right shape.
   It proves nothing about a filesystem.  The following are Runtime or
   Connector obligations that no document validator can observe, and a
   reviewer assessing an implementation must check them another way
   (Appendix H lists them as the gate's own honesty statement):

   *  Sidecar file existence, and the binding between an ordinal and a
      directory entry on disk.

   *  Whether size_bytes and sha256 match the bytes actually on disk.

   *  Display sanitization of filename, and its never-a-path invariant.

   *  The keying of inbound Sidecar directories on the Runtime-minted
      notice identifier.

   *  The location of Runtime-private Staging, outside the mounted
      Volume.

   *  Write ordering and commit-sentinel atomicity.

   *  Caps, allowlists, and quotas.

   *  The absence of a spooled body for a quarantined or blocked
      message.

   *  A Connector's tolerance of a read-only inbound tree.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 55]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  Ingest by copy.

   *  Write-side path discipline, in all three of its conjunctive legs.

   *  Read-side open discipline.

   *  Single writer and single drainer per Namespace.

   *  Compose-time rejection or stripping of CR, LF, and NUL.

   Two of these deserve emphasis as trust-model statements rather than
   as testing notes.  First, disposition == "clean" is the _Runtime's
   assertion_, and this document deliberately does not specify the basis
   for it; a consumer that treats clean as a proof rather than as an
   assertion has misread the trust model.  Second, this protocol cannot
   make a Runtime trustworthy — it can only ensure that everything the
   Agent contributes is inert until a Runtime acts on it, and that
   whatever the Runtime asserts is legible and attributable to the
   Runtime.

12.15.  The extension space, and outcomes as claims

   outbound/ext/<name>/ (Section 4.1) is Connector-owned and Agent-
   writable, and this document specifies no shape for anything under it.
   Its <name> is a stable, opaque Connector id (Section 4.1), so a
   Runtime's out-of-band agreement with a Connector survives that
   Connector's repository being renamed.  Nothing security-relevant may
   be built on it.  Its first use, a per-Notice outcome file, is written
   by the receiving Agent's own uid and is therefore forgeable by
   construction: a receiving Agent can claim a delivery that did not
   happen, deny one that did, or suppress a refusal.  An outcome is a
   statement by the receiving side about what it did with a Notice; a
   party MUST NOT treat an outcome as proof of delivery or of non-
   delivery, and the Runtime's own delivery record is authoritative over
   it.  A Runtime that reads outcomes may let them change what a sender
   is told or what an operator sees; it MUST NOT let them change what
   its own record says happened.  There is deliberately no inbound
   extension space, because an inbound tree is a Runtime assertion about
   origin (Section 7.1) and a Connector cannot know what a vendor-named
   assertion means.

13.  IANA Considerations

   This document has no IANA actions.

   _(Normative.)_ The schema below is written in the JSON Schema 2020-12
   dialect [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12] and governs the artifact defined in
   Section 5.  This is the Agent-authored artifact, and its envelope is
   closed at every level: an unrecognized member is a hard rejection,
   surfaced as a rejected Result rather than as a silent drop
   (Section 11.1).

Appendix B.  Result Schema

   _(Normative.)_ JSON Schema 2020-12 [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12]; governs the
   artifact defined in Section 6.  Runtime-authored, and therefore open
   at every level: a consumer tolerates unrecognized members
   (Section 11.1).  The attachments[i].index == i binding stated in
   Section 6.1 is not expressible here and is enforced as a named post-
   check by the conformance gate (Appendix H).

   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   {
     "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
     "$id": "https://amap-spec/schemas/result.schema.json",
     "title": "result",
     "description": "runtime -> agent: verdict for a submit-request. am\
       ap-spec v3.0.0 (spec/contract.md §4). Runtime-authored: this doc\
       ument's envelope is OPEN (no additionalProperties:false) at ever\
       y level per §7's v3.0.0 tolerance rule — a consumer MUST ignore \
       members it does not recognize; emitting an unrecognized member r\
       emains producer non-conformance.",
     "type": "object",
     "required": ["contract_version", "req_id", "outcome"],
     "properties": {
       "contract_version": { "const": "2" },

Appendix C.  Deliver-Notice Schema

   _(Normative.)_ JSON Schema 2020-12 [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12]; governs the
   artifact defined in Section 7.  Runtime-authored and open at every
   level.  The two allOf conditionals implement the clean-gating of
   content_ref and sha256 (Section 7.2); the content_ref index and
   prefix binding, by contrast, is not expressible here and is enforced
   as a named post-check (Appendix H).

Appendix F.  Peer-Notice Schema (v3.1.0 DRAFT)

   _(Normative for the shape it pins; the profile it belongs to is
   DRAFT.)_ JSON Schema 2020-12 [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12]; governs a peer
   notice, the artifact the peer-origin profile places under <agent-
   id>/peer/notices/. The profile's prose is a companion document (spec/
   peer-origin.md, v3.1.0 DRAFT); at this document version the schema
   and the peer-* fixtures (Appendix H) are the whole of what this
   document specifies about it.  The envelope is Runtime-authored and
   therefore open (Section 11.1).  A document with kind: "peer" found
   under inbound/notices/ fails the deliver-notice schema (Appendix C),
   and a document with kind: "deliver" found under peer/notices/ fails
   this one; both are dropped under the rule of Section 7.1.

Appendix G.  Golden Examples

   _(Normative.)_ The documents below are reproduced byte-verbatim from
   the conformance suite (Appendix H).  They are a small selection
   covering each artifact type and three rejections; the suite itself is
   the authority.  The selection is configured in draft/fixtures.toml,
   not hardcoded in this document's build tooling, and one further
   example — a Binding Record — is shown inline at Section 9 instead of
   being repeated here.

G.1.  Valid Submit Request with attachments

   Sidecar blobs are named by array index (req-<id>.attachments/<i>); no
   content_ref may appear on a request and the schema rejects one
   (Section 5.1).

   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "req_id": "00000010",
     "agent_id": "agent.research",
     "ts": "2026-07-21T04:10:00Z",
     "draft": {
       "to": ["owner@example.com"],
       "subject": "Report attached",
       "body_text": "See the attached report and notes.",
       "attachments": [
         { "filename": "report.pdf", "media_type": "application/pdf",
           "size_bytes": 48213,
           "sha256": "970e441b6c4ecd37abf2541e1276c680bdec8481cef9368ff\
       1d010fd6b784b07" },
         { "filename": "notes.txt", "media_type": "text/plain",
           "size_bytes": 128,
           "sha256": "087d07499f2c097ac5396af7a0f1ef5e7a977fa91c631ebd1\
       5eb61bb23ef20aa" }
       ]
     }
   }

             Figure 14: fixtures/valid/request-attachments.json






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 70]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


G.2.  Valid Deliver Notice with a clean attachment Descriptor

   content_ref's prefix equals the enclosing document's own notice_id
   and its trailing index equals the Descriptor's own array position
   (Section 7.2); a Connector that relays the Notice without ever
   dereferencing the reference is fully conformant.

   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "notice_id": "1721457600000000003-4242",
     "ts": "2026-07-21T04:06:00Z",
     "kind": "deliver",
     "message": {
       "id": "45",
       "from": "colleague@example.com",
       "subject": "Clean attachment (deferred-release wire shape)",
       "preview": "byte-access forward-valid example",
       "mailbox": "inbox",
       "attachments": [
         { "filename": "photo.jpg", "media_type": "image/jpeg",
           "size_bytes": 204800,
           "sha256": "04c22051bc3f76bc44b952d9fdd3e59214662e7b3fd8a84b8\
       9de09352aeb2264",
           "disposition": "clean",
           "content_ref": "1721457600000000003-4242.attachments/0" }
       ]
     }
   }

         Figure 15: fixtures/valid/notice-attachment-clean-ref.json

G.3.  Valid Inbound Message

   The body spool for a delivered message is keyed on the Runtime-minted
   notice_id, never on the provider message.id (Section 7.3).














Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 71]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "notice_id": "1721457600000000000-4242",
     "id": "42",
     "date": "Mon, 20 Jul 2026 04:00:00 +0000",
     "from": "Alex Doe <owner@example.com>",
     "to": "agent@example.org",
     "subject": "status?",
     "body_text": "hey, how's the run going",
     "attachments": [
       { "filename": "report.pdf", "media_type": "application/pdf",
         "size_bytes": 48213, "disposition": "unscanned" }
     ]
   }

                Figure 16: fixtures/valid/message-clean.json

G.4.  Valid Result — a policy hold with per-attachment diagnostics

   attachments[i].index == i on a Result, contiguous and unique over
   0..n-1; per-attachment entries are diagnostic detail under one
   governing top-level outcome and never license a partial send
   (Section 6.1).

   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "req_id": "00000010",
     "outcome": "queued_for_human",
     "detail": "no outbound screener wired; attachments fail-closed to \
       human review",
     "recipients": ["owner@example.com"],
     "message_id": null,
     "job_id": null,
     "attachments": [
       { "index": 0, "outcome": "dlp_held", "detail": "no verdict sourc\
       e" },
       { "index": 1, "outcome": "dlp_held", "detail": "no verdict sourc\
       e" }
     ]
   }

           Figure 17: fixtures/valid/result-attachments-held.json







Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 72]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


G.5.  Invalid Deliver Notice — a content_ref that fails the binding

   The drop rule of Section 7.1 is two independent checks: this document
   is schema-valid and is caught only by the content_ref post-check
   (Section 7.2, Section 11.3).

   content_ref names a different notice's Sidecar directory and a non-
   matching index — it is neither <notice_id>.attachments/0 for its own
   array position 0, nor prefixed by this document's own notice_id.
   Schema validation alone reports zero errors; only the content_ref
   index/prefix post-check catches it.

   The conformance gate's own errors for this document:

   $.attachments[0].content_ref: 'OTHER-NOTICE.attachments/7' !=
     'n-index-mismatch.attachments/0'

   {
     "contract_version": "2",
     "notice_id": "n-index-mismatch",
     "ts": "2026-07-21T04:06:00Z",
     "kind": "deliver",
     "message": {
       "id": "46",
       "from": "colleague@example.com",
       "subject": "wrong content_ref",
       "preview": "descriptor points at another notice's sidecar",
       "mailbox": "inbox",
       "attachments": [
         { "filename": "photo.jpg", "media_type": "image/jpeg",
           "size_bytes": 204800,
           "disposition": "clean",
           "content_ref": "OTHER-NOTICE.attachments/7" }
       ]
     }
   }

   Figure 18: fixtures/invalid/notice-attachment-ref-index-mismatch.json

   The Runtime-authored envelope is OPEN as of document version 3.0.0: a
   consumer MUST ignore a member it does not recognize, at every level
   (Section 11.1).

G.7.  Invalid Submit Request carrying an unrecognized member

   The Agent-authored envelope stays CLOSED at every level: an
   unrecognized member is a designed, legible rejected refusal, never a
   silent drop (Section 11.1).

   additionalProperties: false at the top level of the submit-request
   schema rejects any member this document does not define.

   The conformance gate's own errors for this document:

   $: additional property 'x_injected' not allowed

   NOTE: '\' line wrapping per RFC 8792

   { "contract_version": "2", "req_id": "00000021", "x_injected": "surp\
       rise",
     "draft": { "to": ["a@b"], "subject": "s", "body_text": "b" } }

            Figure 20: fixtures/invalid/request-extra-field.json

G.8.  Invalid peer notice — a deliver-kind document under the peer tree

   Origin class comes from the tree a notice arrived in, never from a
   self-declared field: a kind: "deliver" document found under peer/
   notices/ fails the peer-notice schema, the profile's cross-lock
   (spec/peer-origin.md).

   kind is const "peer" in the peer-notice schema; a document carrying
   "deliver" fails that const check.

   The conformance gate's own errors for this document:

   $.kind: 'deliver' != const 'peer'

       39e04", "ts": "t", "kind": "deliver",
     "message": { "id": "9f1c2b7e4d3a4f60b8e2c1d5a7f39e04", "from": "pl\

                                  Table 4

   *Running it.* The validator is stdlib-only and takes no arguments:

   python3 fixtures/validate.py

   It exits 0 if and only if every fixture under valid/ passes and every
   fixture under invalid/ fails.  It requires no counterpart, no
   network, and no dependency: *the fixtures are the other side.*

   *How a fixture is mapped to a schema.* By filename prefix — request-
   to the submit-request schema, notice- to deliver-notice, result- to
   result, message- to inbound-message, identity- to binding-record, and
   peer- to peer-notice (Appendix F).

   *What the validator checks.* Schema validation in the JSON Schema
   2020-12 dialect [JSON-SCHEMA-2020-12], over the subset of keywords
   these schemas use (type, const, enum, minLength, pattern, minItems,
   minimum, items, required, properties, additionalProperties, allOf,
   and a single if/then pair) — plus two *named post-checks*, neither
   expressible in standard JSON Schema:

   *  the Result-side binding attachments[i].index == i, contiguous and
      unique over 0 through n-1 (Section 6.1);






Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 80]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  the content_ref index and prefix binding on Notice, Inbound
      Message, and peer-notice documents: every Descriptor carrying
      content_ref must equal <notice_id>.attachments/<i> for its own
      array position i, binding both the trailing index and the leading
      prefix (Section 7.2).

   A Connector conformance claim requires running *both* the schema
   validation and the second post-check, because exactly one invalid
   notice-* fixture — and its peer-* counterpart — is schema-valid on
   its own and is caught only by that post-check (Appendix G,
   Section 11.3).

   *A note on pattern anchoring, and a portability cost.* Every schema
   pattern in this suite that ends in $ is written as (?!\n)$. The
   reason is that a bare $ matches before a single trailing newline in
   several widely used regex engines — Python's re, Java, and .NET among
   them — unlike the ECMA-262 dialect JSON Schema specifies.  Since
   every one of these patterns exists to forbid exactly the control
   characters a permissive $ would let through at the end of a string,
   the lookahead closes that gap in the schemas themselves rather than
   in any one validator.  Seven fixtures pin the trailing-newline case
   specifically, distinct from the CRLF fixtures, which embed \r\n and
   were already rejected even under a permissive engine.

   The cost is disclosed rather than discovered: *lookahead-less engines
   cannot compile these patterns at all.* RE2 (Go's regexp), Rust's
   regex crate, and POSIX ERE reject (?! outright, so the three schemas
   carrying the guard fail to load rather than validating loosely.
   Those engines already treat $ as strict end-of-string and never had
   the gap, so an implementer on one of them should strip the lookahead
   — not add a check outside the pattern, which would be both
   unnecessary and not what breaks.  The failure is loud (a compile
   error, never silent acceptance).

   *What a green run proves.* That every document shape this protocol
   defines is accepted or rejected as specified, by an implementation's
   own parser, with no counterpart present.

   *What a green run does NOT prove.* The following are filesystem and
   policy invariants that no document validator can observe.  They are
   obligations of the conformance classes regardless (Section 11.3), and
   are checked operationally:

   *  Sidecar file existence — an extra file, a missing file, or a
      directory present when the Descriptor array is empty or absent.

   *  size_bytes and sha256 actually matching the bytes on disk.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 81]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  filename display-sanitization, and the "never a path" invariant.

   *  The binding between an ordinal and a directory entry on disk.  The
      schema checks only the _Descriptor_ array's own index member, not
      that directory entry N exists.

   *  Inbound Sidecar directories keyed on the Runtime-minted notice
      identifier rather than the provider message.id.

   *  The location of Runtime-private Staging, outside the mounted
      Volume.

   *  Write ordering and commit-sentinel atomicity — Sidecars before
      req-<id>.json; .tmp plus rename.

   *  Caps and allowlists — type allowlists, size caps, Volume quotas.

   *  The absence of a spooled body for a quarantined or blocked message
      (enforcement by absence, Section 7.3).

   *  A Connector's tolerance of a read-only inbound/ tree.  The
      prescribed check is operational, not a fixture: run the Connector
      against an inbound tree it cannot write and confirm that it
      starts, relays every pending Notice, resolves bodies, and submits
      outbound requests, without requiring any inbound write to succeed
      (Section 11.3).

   *  Ingest by copy — validation, policy evaluation, and composition
      running over a Runtime-private snapshot taken before any of those
      steps, rather than re-reading an Agent-writable path
      (Section 4.1).

   *  Write-side path discipline, all three conjunctive legs: full
      parent-chain resolution through pinned directory descriptors from
      the Namespace root; each directory component opened
      O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY at the moment it is added to that chain;
      and the final component created O_EXCL and never followed, failing
      closed on EEXIST and ELOOP.  Any one leg alone is a known-
      insufficient partial mitigation (Section 4.1).

   *  Read-side open discipline — per-component no-symlink-follow opens,
      non-blocking opens, fstat-based regular-file verification through
      the open descriptor, and bounded reads and caps on every Agent-
      influenced path (Section 4.1).

   *  Single writer and single drainer per Namespace — an operational
      and deployment invariant, such as an OS-level lock held for the
      process lifetime (Section 4.1).



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 82]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  Compose-time header-boundary stripping: even where the schemas'
      control-character patterns are bypassed upstream, the Runtime
      rejects or strips CR, LF, and NUL before composing the outbound
      message (Section 5.1).

   *  The peer-origin profile's operational obligations (v3.1.0 DRAFT),
      none of them visible to a document validator: the write-authority
      partition — no component that admits messages from a transport not
      restricted to authorised peer senders holds write authority over
      peer/, and the prescribed check is a write attempt from inside the
      admitting component that must fail; intake isolation for shared-
      transport peer candidates, in a location that is neither inbound/
      nor peer/ and unreachable from any Agent Namespace; verification
      placement in a component holding peer write authority that hashes
      body and attachment bytes itself; sender_exposure never sender-
      settable; a peer notice carrying in_reply_to only when the placing
      Runtime resolved it from its own record, an unresolvable key being
      refused rather than stripped; and at-most-once action by the
      Connector, with an ambiguous target held rather than fanned out.

   Beyond these, the behavioral obligations of Sections 7 and 8 — the
   untrusted-content posture, the treatment of task_id as correlation
   rather than authorization, and the requirement that verified sender
   identity never be taken from message.from — sit outside the fixture
   gate entirely.  They constrain what an implementation _does_ with a
   valid document, which no document-level gate can see.

Appendix I.  A Deferred Seam-Visible "Handled" Signal (Non-Normative)

   *This appendix is non-normative and is not in force at this document
   version.* It records the reasoning behind a gap deliberately left
   open, not an addition to the protocol.  Nothing below is a directory,
   a member, or an artifact that a conforming implementation can rely
   on, and no requirement keyword appears anywhere in it.

   *The gap.* Making inbound consumption-tracking Connector-private
   (Section 4.1) closes the writability conflict but leaves a knowledge
   and capability split unbridged: only the Connector knows that a
   Notice has been relayed to its Agent, while on a read-only inbound
   tree only the Runtime can delete anything.  Neither side alone can
   turn "consumed" into "reclaimed."

   *A sketch, not a specification.* One shape that would bridge it is a
   Connector-written, zero-byte marker per acknowledged Notice, written
   into outbound/, where the Connector already has write access in every
   posture:

   outbound/acks/notice-<id>   # sketch only - not part of the protocol



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 83]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


             Figure 22: Sketch only — not part of this protocol

   A Runtime could then delete the acknowledged Notice and its spooled
   message, and finally the marker itself.  This is presented purely as
   a sketch: no directory and no wire member is introduced by this
   appendix.

   *Why a Connector-forgeable signal would be acceptable here.* A
   garbage-collection signal is a resource decision rather than a
   security decision.  An Agent that falsely claims consumption loses
   only its own unread mail; one that never claims consumption only
   bloats its own inbox.  Neither crosses a trust boundary that matters,
   and neither touches any record of the exchange the Runtime keeps on
   its own side.  That is what distinguishes this case from every other
   "the Agent writes it, so it cannot be trusted" case in this document
   — but it is a distinction a future version would need to state
   explicitly rather than assume.

   *Why a high-water mark cannot substitute.* Section 8 requires task_id
   to be unguessable and never sequential, and nothing in this document
   orders notice identifiers, so no single "processed through N" cursor
   is expressible.  Any consumption signal has to be a _set_ of
   identifiers, or time-ordered — and time-ordering would require the
   consumer to process strictly in delivery order, which nothing today
   requires.

   *The lifecycle this would enable, and its boundaries.* A reliable "is
   this one done?" answer is the watermark a real retention lifecycle
   promotes against: cycling a working set, rolling handled traffic into
   period-compacted archives, then expiring or tiering to cold storage.
   Three boundaries would need to hold if this is ever specified.

   *  *The seam is not the record.* A Runtime that needs an exchange of
      record already keeps one outside this protocol, tamper-evident.
      Retention here is about an Agent's access to its own history, not
      about the durability of evidence; conflating the two produces an
      archive that satisfies neither.

   *  *An Agent-writable archive is never evidence.* A compacted archive
      living under outbound/, which is Agent-writable in every posture,
      can be rewritten by the Agent it belongs to.  Anything meant to be
      relied on has to be Runtime-written or kept outside this protocol
      entirely.

   *  *It must not grow the read surface.* The read available today is a
      point lookup from a notice identifier to a body.  "Search my
      archive" is a materially larger capability — decompression,
      indexing, query — for a deliberately dumb, credential-free relay



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 84]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


      to take on.  If archives are ever exposed to an Agent, that likely
      belongs behind a Runtime-served surface rather than the file-drop
      seam.

   *Why this is deferred rather than specified now.* A capability starts
   with a change to this document once a second implementation
   independently wants it, with members and fixtures proposed together.
   Today exactly one reference Connector carries a private workaround
   for the underlying problem — a writability-probing fallback with
   three modes: move, ledger, and in-memory.  There is no second data
   point yet to generalize from, and specifying now would freeze one
   side's convention as the protocol's answer.

   *One honesty note for a future implementer.* The sketch's own
   garbage-collection step is not atomic: if a Runtime crashes between
   deleting the Notice artifacts and deleting the acknowledgment marker,
   the marker is orphaned, pointing at a Notice that no longer exists.
   Any real design needs idempotent collection, in which a missing
   target is not an error — recorded here so that it is not rediscovered
   from scratch.

Change Log

   _(Informative.  One entry per document version, newest first, derived
   from the versioning record of the protocol contract this document
   renders.)_

3.1.0 (DRAFT) — the protocol is AMAP; the outbound extension space; the
peer-origin profile's schema

   An additive *minor* bump; the wire major stays "2".

   *  *The protocol is AMAP; the schema $id authority is amap-spec*
      (2026-09-15).  The protocol formerly called AMP ("Agent Mailbox
      Protocol") is renamed AMAP ("Agent Mailbox Access Protocol")
      because AMP collides with the IETF DTN working group's adopted
      draft-ietf-dtn-amp; the specification repository moves from agent-
      mailbox-protocol to amap-spec with it.  The six schema $id values
      move from https://agent-mailbox-protocol/schemas/… to
      https://amap-spec/schemas/…. Nothing on the wire changes shape: no
      document carries the protocol's name as a field, and $id is an
      identifier the gate never dereferences.  Implementations that
      mirror the Runtime's address spell its local part amap.router from
      this version.  This draft's filename is a separate decision and is
      unchanged here.  This version is marked DRAFT: its profile prose
      is a companion document (spec/peer-origin.md, itself DRAFT), and
      its schema and fixtures may still change before it is settled.




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 85]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *Outbound extension space.* outbound/ext/<name>/ is defined as a
      Connector-owned side channel a Runtime MAY read by out-of-band
      agreement, with no shape specified and nothing security-relevant
      permitted to depend on it (Section 4.1). <name> is pinned as a
      stable Connector id — chosen once, unchanged by any rename of the
      Connector's repository, package, or deployment, and opaque to the
      Runtime that reads it; the wording it replaced ("a Connector or
      deployment name") permitted a repository name to leak into a wire-
      visible path.  The first id is claude-code.  One normative
      clarification sits beside it: an outcome written there is a claim
      by the receiving side, never proof of delivery or of non-delivery,
      and the Runtime's own delivery record is authoritative over it
      (Section 12.15).  There is deliberately no inbound extension
      space.

   *  *Peer-notice schema.* The peer-origin profile's artifact is pinned
      by peer-notice.schema.json (Appendix F): the deliver-notice layout
      with kind and mailbox fixed to peer, message.from a bare addr-
      spec, message identifiers in the notice-identifier character set,
      and the optional Runtime-asserted sender_exposure stamp with its
      required members.  The profile's prose is the companion document
      spec/peer-origin.md (v3.1.0 DRAFT).

   *  *Fixtures: 75 total (27 valid, 48 invalid), up from 58.* 16 peer-*
      fixtures were added (6 valid, 10 invalid), covering a minimal
      notice, a reply, the exposure stamp asserted both ways, a clean
      attachment reference, an unknown-member case, and rejections for a
      deliver kind under the peer tree, a peer kind under the inbound
      tree, a display-name or CRLF from, encoded message identifiers, a
      missing asserted_by, a missing last-delivery timestamp when
      exposure is asserted true, an inbox mailbox, a content_ref index
      mismatch, and a trailing-newline identifier.  The validator maps
      the peer- prefix to the new schema and applies the content_ref
      post-check to it.  Three existing fixtures had example strings
      normalised to example.* identities (one free-text body, two
      addresses in injection examples); each stays valid or invalid for
      the same reason as before, and no schema changed.

3.0.0 — direction-aware tolerance, and six closed safety holes

   A *major document bump*; the wire major stays "2".  Section 11.1
   states why the two numbers diverge here, and why bumping the wire
   would have caused the exact harm this version exists to repair.

   *  *Unknown-member tolerance, direction-aware.* The three Runtime-
      authored artifacts — deliver-notice, inbound-message, and result —
      became *open* at every level: additionalProperties: false was
      removed from the top level, from message, from Descriptor items,



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 86]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


      and from attestation, and a consumer must tolerate an unrecognized
      member.  Emitting one remains producer non-conformance.  The
      Agent-authored submit-request envelope stays *closed* at every
      level.  Consequence: adding an optional member to a Runtime-
      authored artifact is now genuinely additive; adding any member to
      the submit-request is a major change.

   *  *...and for values.* The enum constraint was removed from
      message.sender_standing and message.provenance, the two explicitly
      advisory vocabularies, and a consumer must tolerate an
      unrecognized value in either. kind, outcome (both levels), and
      disposition remain closed, enum-locked vocabularies.

   *  *Ingest by copy.* A Runtime must copy an Agent-authored request
      and its Sidecars into private staging before validating, must act
      only on that copy, and must not re-read an Agent-writable path
      after a decision depending on its content (Section 4.1).

   *  *Address syntax and header-injection discipline.* A new obligation
      in Section 5.1 plus schema patterns on draft.to/cc, draft.subject,
      attachment filename and media_type, draft.reply_to_message_id,
      in_reply_to, agent_id, and ts — including the two members composed
      directly into headers, which earlier schema coverage missed.

   *  *Path discipline, write- and read-side both.* The write-side rule
      became *conjunctive* (Section 4.1), and a new read-side rule
      applies the equivalent discipline to every Agent-influenceable
      read.  A notice_id character-set pattern was added to the deliver-
      notice and inbound-message schemas so that every legal notice_id
      is also a legal content_ref prefix. *Disclosed cost:* notice_id
      was previously unconstrained, so a Runtime minting identifiers
      outside the new character set — an ISO-8601 timestamp, standard
      base64, a URN, or anything else carrying punctuation outside it —
      now emits Notices and Inbound Messages that fail schema validation
      on a _pattern violation on a required member_, and a conforming
      Connector drops them. *Migration:* such a Runtime must re-mint
      identifiers under the new character set (unpadded base64url or
      lowercase hex, for instance) before any Connector it talks to
      upgrades, because the failure is otherwise silent on both sides.

   *  *Single writer, single drainer.* Section 4.1 now names the
      concurrency assumption that every atomicity, commit-sentinel, and
      req_id rule already depended on.

   *  *message.from named untrusted.* The untrusted-content sentence now
      covers explicitly the member most likely to be rendered to a human
      or used for a trust judgement (Section 7.1).




Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 87]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   *  *Document authority.* The contract, its schemas, and its fixtures
      are normative; this rendering is generated from them and is non-
      authoritative where they disagree.  The conformance-class text was
      moved into the contract itself so that the demotion deletes
      nothing, and a stray claim of a second, message-specific Sidecar
      directory was corrected to match the layout tree.

   *  *Corrections shipped with this version*, rather than a tidied
      history: (i) the write rule described in an earlier revision as
      "strengthened" had in fact been weakened — the exclusive-create
      requirement on the final component had been deleted rather than
      supplemented (Section 11.1); (ii) the inbound drop rule described
      as a pure closure over schema validation was refuted by this
      version's own content_ref-binding fixture, and is now stated as
      two independent checks (Section 7.1, Section 11.3); (iii) the
      claim that this version's producer bytes are unchanged is
      explicitly _not_ made — two producer-side narrowings are disclosed
      above, each travelling a legible per-artifact refusal path; and
      (iv) the 2.1.0 entry below is corrected in place.

   *  *Fixtures: 58 total (21 valid, 37 invalid), up from 44.* The
      unknown-member notice fixture moved from the invalid set to the
      valid set and was extended with an unrecognized member inside
      message; valid unknown-member fixtures were added for result and
      inbound-message; the withheld-body invalid fixture was deleted,
      having become schema-valid under the relaxed envelope (its name
      always over-claimed what additionalProperties alone tested); the
      bad-provenance fixture moved to the valid set as an unrecognized-
      value case; an invalid extra-member submit-request fixture was
      added to pin the closed side of the asymmetry, previously untested
      at the top level; four invalid fixtures were added for the
      address-syntax and control-character rules; a traversal notice_id
      fixture was added; the content_ref index-mismatch fixture was
      added, and is the one invalid notice-* case that is schema-valid
      on its own; and six fixtures pin the trailing-newline anchoring
      case.

2.3.0 — inbound byte access in force

   A *minor bump*, prose only: no schema rule and no fixture changed,
   and the wire major stayed "2".  It resolved an inconsistency carried
   since 2.0.0.  A fixture showing a clean Descriptor with content_ref
   and sha256 sat in the valid set as a deliberately forward-valid
   shape, while the prose forbade any Runtime from producing it — the
   gate blessed what the prose forbade.  This version sided with the
   fixtures: the release-scoped byte embargo was dropped, and the
   standing rule became the one stated in Section 7.2 — a Runtime may
   publish bytes and emit content_ref/sha256 only for a Descriptor it



Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 88]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


   asserts clean, and a Runtime that cannot make that determination must
   not assert clean.  The substantive clarification is that disposition
   is the Runtime's _assertion_, its basis deliberately unspecified; the
   older prose presumed a scanner, which is what made byte access read
   as a deferred capability rather than as a policy decision whose wire
   shape major 2 already carried.  Nothing was tightened, and there is
   still no outbound content_ref.

2.2.0 — deletion rights, read-only inbound

   A *permissive minor bump*: no wire member, no schema change, no
   fixture changed or added.  It (a) declared a read-only inbound tree a
   valid Runtime posture and made the inbound processed/ archive
   directory optional, (b) obliged a Connector not to require inbound
   write access, making consumption-recording Connector-private, and (c)
   named deletion rights per artifact class, along with the two
   constraints attached to them: a Connector must not delete or rewrite
   a published request, and a Connector exercising its new deletion
   rights must preserve req_id monotonicity by other durable means.  It
   also pinned three previously implicit reason_code rules: setting one
   on every Result became a keyworded SHOULD, and a consumer must
   tolerate an unrecognized code and must not infer outcome from it.

2.1.0 — the body spool, and three optional Result members

   Recorded at the time as an *additive minor bump*: one new optional
   spooled artifact (the Inbound Message) and its schema, one new
   optional Notice member (provenance), and three new optional Result
   members (reason_code, attestation, ts).  No existing schema gained a
   required member, no existing fixture changed shape, and the wire
   major stayed "2".

   *Correction (recorded at 3.0.0).* That "additive minor" label was
   unsound as written.  Against a strictly validating 2.0.0 consumer —
   every schema at that version was closed at every level — a Notice
   carrying the new provenance member failed schema validation as a
   *whole document* and was silently dropped: precisely the failure mode
   cited as the reason attachments had required a major bump,
   reintroduced as a minor.  Version 3.0.0 repairs the versioning model
   rather than relabelling this history, which is why this entry still
   records what shipped rather than what would have been correct.










Rapp & Adams              Expires 20 March 2027                [Page 89]

Internet-Draft                    AMAP                    September 2026


2.0.0 — attachments, and contract_version required

   A *major bump*, moving the wire major from "1" to "2".  It added
   attachment support in both directions — outbound Descriptors with
   required size_bytes and sha256 and their Sidecar bytes, inbound
   Descriptors with a disposition — and made contract_version REQUIRED
   on the submit-request, deliver-notice, and result artifacts, with no
   compatibility mode.  The reason the bump had to be major rather than
   minor is the reasoning in Section 11.1: under the then-universal
   closed envelopes, a new member caused a major-1 consumer to reject
   the _whole document_, which inbound is silent total message loss.  A
   version signal, rather than an unknown-member rejection, is what
   makes that refusal legible.

Fixture identifier normalization

   Across these versions the fixture suite's identities were normalized
   to example.com and example.org placeholders, and deployment-specific
   identifiers were removed from fixture content.  This changed no shape
   and no expectation: every affected fixture validates exactly as
   before, and no identifier removed in that pass is reintroduced by
   this document.
